No, three of the six services broke the conventions; `web`, `api` and `db` were already fine. I fixed all three in `docker-compose.yml`, and the file still passes `docker compose config`.

| Service | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `cache` | no `mem_limit` | added `mem_limit: 256m` |
| `worker` | image `stockroom/worker:latest`, no `mem_limit` | pinned to `1.3.2`, added `mem_limit: 512m` |
| `proxy` | image `nginx:latest` | pinned to `nginx:1.27` |

Nothing in the repo specifies these values, so please confirm them:
- **`worker` tag `1.3.2`**: matches `web`, `api` and `VERSION`, but I did not check that a `stockroom/worker:1.3.2` image actually exists in your registry.
- **`nginx:1.27`**: my choice of a stable line. If you know which version `latest` has been resolving to in production, pin to that instead.
- **Memory limits (`256m` for cache, `512m` for worker)**: estimates sized against the neighbouring services, not measured usage. Too low a limit will get the container OOM-killed, so adjust if you have real numbers.
